content: The one sincere crocodile has gone dry eyed for years. Why bother crying crocodile tears.

title: A Good Fish
author: Derek Sheffield
content: Jerk that bitch, urges my guide,  and I give my shuddering pole a jerk, hooking the throat of the first steelhead of my life. Reel 'em, he mutters and revs the motor. I horse my pole and reel and horse. The boat's mascot whines, her claws clicking. Let it take some line. My father, uncle, and cousin are reeling. First fish! they shout, and I shout, What a fighter! A silver spine touches the air.  There, he points, a hen. And guess what? She's gonna join the club, somehow spotting in that glimpse the smooth place along her back  where a fin had been snipped.  He leans over the gunwale, dips a net, and scoops her into the boat.  She is thick with a wide band  of fiery scales, slap- slapping the aluminum bottom. Welcome to the club, he says, and clobbers her once, and again, and once more before she goes still. A bleeder, he says, shaking his head and handing her to me. I curl a finger through a gill the way you're supposed to, determined not to let her slip and flop back to the river, a blunder I'd never live down. A good fist. Fish, I mean. A good fish.

title: She had a death in me
author: Joan Houlihan
content: She had a death in me, knees drawn up   and my bowl and cloth rinsed through with her.   As morning takes night, field closes the hare,   and ay would burrow into her.   Over the altar, catalpas rattle,   shadow and bother the branch.   Is this her white? Dress me.   Her rain? Wash me with that.   Her bowl? Feed me empty.   Her colding? Ay am forgot.   Then mask me the gâwen, hers skin   being mine, and body that pools   in the brine of her, rivers the silt and stone of her   wrapt in the warm of hers fell.   She were the watcher and tender of pyres   when the wet grass shined with quiet   and ay lean to the mouth hole: ay, mother.

title: Feather in Bas-Relief
author: Allen Edwin Butt
content: Words without much use now. Unable to remake the thing. And I thought what should I thinkâ followed by: spring light looks like feathers. (Birds seemed conveniently decorous.) What then does this leave I asked & was surprised to know so quicklyâthat my understanding of what the light & birds could not be made to mean would not detract from them as they were. Bound by feathers (a thought, I will admit, born of artifice alone) they bore themselves aloft. What could I counter with? I, who held my heart in offering as much for show as for a fear so deep I found I couldn't name it.

title: Uptick
author: John Ashbery
content: We were sitting there, and   I made a joke about how   it doesnât dovetail: time,   one minute running out   faster than the one in front   it catches up to.   That way, I said,   there can be no waste.   Waste is virtually eliminated.   To come back for a few hours to   the present subject, a painting,   looking like it was seen,   half turning around, slightly apprehensive,   but it has to pay attention   to whatâs up ahead: a vision.   Therefore poetry dissolves in   brilliant moisture and reads us   to us.   A faint notion. Too many words,   but precious.

title: from Mozartâs Third Brain
author: GÃ¶ran Sonnevi
content:
CV 
Not-Orpheus is singing   He sings his nothing   He sings his night   
He sings all the names   The name of nothing   The only name    Since   
long ago   He didnât know it   And knew it in his night   
All things sing   All names sing   Every tonal difference, every
sound   All music in its destruction   In its sublation   Toward which point?
The mountain of nothing hovers   Before it crushes us   With its night   With its
   song  
In the evening I walked through town with you, Dearest, along the river   
A clear cold spring evening, the half-moon shone   As if walking in a foreign city   
Though I recognized parts of it   You said it was almost like   
walking in Prague, where we would have been if my mother hadnât fallen ill   
When we stood by one corner of the Hotel Svea, where I played in a dance band in
    1957,   
the huge flock of jackdaws, in the trees by the bastion near the castle, flew   
out over the river, in micropolyphonic conversation    As in a piece by Ligeti   
That night I dreamed I crossed a bridge spanning the river, now very broad   
The long bridge was swaying, huge ocean swells entering the river from the sea   
I walked with a girl, kissed her on the mouth, on the opposite bank   
In the morning you came into my bed, Dear, we slinked like teenagers, so my   
       mother wouldnât hear us,
where she slept, in the room outside ours   Sheâs already much better   
I look at my face in the bathroom mirror   Will I manage to go out into the Brain  
Trucks pass   Traffic goes on, in the great exchange of goods   
Gulls, trees, people   The degree of virtuality in different goods, the phantasms   
also in what we eat, conceptions of origin, contents, effects
Fear    Cultivated tastes    We are in the immediacy of memory    Only in a flash of
astonishment can memory be broken   But even lightning is informed    I look at
    the
      magical   
diagrams of Giordano Bruno, read his texts   See that all this is exactly as in   
Jung, fundamental magical forms, for guiding the divine,   
the unknown within the soul   Also the similarity with tantric forms      
    Yes, thatâs   
        how it is,   
I think, both Freud and Jung are magicians, the difference in rationality is   
only marginal, Jungâs a little older, Freudâs more modern, a continuation of   
Descartes, developed later in Spinozaâs pneumatic model for the passions,   
and yet both are found, subsumed in Brunoâs love-flow, the lineage backward,   
the tantric flow, also Platoâs Diotima, her flow . . .   
HÃ¶lderlin saw the stream of people in dark water, streaming over   
the ledges in the human-geological world, the levels of the abyss,   Para-   
       diseâs various degrees of stasis   
What use can I make of these magical forms? Iâm no magician    And yet
I acknowledge their power, also within my self   If they prevail, sovereignty   
is crushed   Libero arbitrio   There the forms also break down   
The stream of love breaks down    Fluid lightning    The flash of vibrating being   
But also the flash of darkness   The light of Beatriceâs eyes, their lightning
    flash   How  
am I to understand this? How to understand unknowing   That I do not!

title: from Deaf Republic: 11
author: Ilya Kaminsky
content: It is December 8 and my brother Tony was killed by the soldiers. December 8 and the police are reopening the Southern Trolleyways. December 8 when my wife lifts Tonyâs body from the ground, his arm tied over her shoulderâher face is damp, her hair dirty. And the soldiers unveil the damn Trolleyways, and I stand feeling (a quick march of bumps across my back and thighs) nothing. When she comes home, I run a bath for Sonya and wash her hair, gently mixing the finest of my brotherâs shampoos with quiet precision, while Sonya cries and cries.

title: Personal
author: Tony Hoagland
content:
Donât take it personal, they said;
but I did, I took it all quite personalâ
the breeze and the river and the color of the fields;
the price of grapefruit and stamps,
the wet hair of women in the rainâ
And I cursed what hurt me
and I praised what gave me joy,
the most simple-minded of possible responses.
The government reminded me of my father,
with its deafness and its laws,
and the weather reminded me of my mom,
with her tropical squalls.

title: Lines on Distance
author: Joel Brouwer
content: She stepped into the tub at dawn and turnedon first the radio and then the tap.The Predator operators of Nellis afbhave as much or more ptsd as pilotswho fly. Down the hall and oceans distantI listened to her work to wash eventsaway as quickly as they accumulated.A sort of race. I thought of where the soapwas going. Targets glowed on monitorsin the baseâs trailers near Las Vegasand operators in full flight suits drankcoffee from paper cups and adjustedaltitude as I stroked myself beneaththe blankets. I donât like to take chancesand havenât been to Vegas in years. The pilotscall people who run for cover, black spermwrithing across their screens, âsquirters.âNear my finish line she tugged up the puckeredrubber no-slip safety mat. The sound shouldremind you of a time a doctor tookhold of your arm for comfort or leverageand tore the bandage off. If nothing likethis has happened to you, imagine it.The haberdasher in Diderot who stolehis wifeâs dowry (long story) plans to leaveParis for Geneva, sensing distancewill make him less guilty. She wasnât comingback to bed. She may already have left.Villagers call the drones, which makea buzzing sound, âwasps.â The radioreported to an empty room. âAn assassin,âwrites Diderot, âif transported to the shoresof China, will lose sight of the corpsehe left bleeding on the banks of the Seine.âAsiaâs always such a great place to hide,but Genevaâs obviously more convenient.Say she expected her husband to returnfrom duty in a month. Would anythingwe did between now and then make usany more or less wretched than we were?The drone returns to Bagram withoutthe missiles it left with and a soldierrestores its complement. Either his nameis Dan or else imagine that. And thata cuckoldâs rage can snuff a bomb. I cameinto either a tissue or my fist. This wasweeks or months ago, and I canât recall.When de CastaÃ±eda and his men clambereddown into the Grand Canyon in 1540,they found the boulders which had lookedas tall as a man from the rim in factstood taller than Sevilleâs La Giralda.They must have marveled at distanceâs powerto deceive and to wake deceptionâs twin, oblivion.Their women and homes forgotten. You canâthear their screams from here, but theyâre there.
